result: A simplified, highly efficient CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in strategy was established in medaka using PCR-amplified donor fragments with short homology arms (30-40 bp), biotinylated 5' ends, and Cas9-mSA. Eight genes were targeted with various fluorescent proteins, achieving F0 targeting efficiency of 11-59% mosaic expression and germline transmission of 25-100%. Eight stable KI lines were established, with 7/8 requiring only a single injection round.
evaluation: Claims C3-C32 collectively demonstrate the establishment and efficiency of the method through experimental data showing successful generation of multiple lines with quantified targeting and germline transmission rates (C23, C25, C26, C27, C28). Control experiments (C24) validate the requirement for homology arms. The methodology is well-documented (C4, C14, C18-C21) and advantages are clearly stated (C20, C21, C32).

result: Initial comparison of different Cas9 designs (with/without mSA tag, with/without biotinylation) showed comparable KI efficiencies in F0s. Cas9 with only one NLS showed lower efficiency and lethality compared to Cas9 with two NLSs.
evaluation: Claims C30, C124, C125 present preliminary comparative data but acknowledge that further evaluation is needed (C124). The comparison is described as 'initial' with limited scope (F0 screening only), and the authors explicitly state the benefit of the mSA/Biotin system needs further evaluation. Sample sizes and statistical analysis are not provided.

result: Whole genome sequencing with high coverage and Sanger sequencing validated precise single-copy integration at targeted loci. WGS of three lines (eGFP-cbx1b, mScarlet-pcna, mNeonGreen-myosinhc) showed fluorescent protein reads only at endogenous target loci. Sanger sequencing of seven lines confirmed in-frame fusion proteins with only 2/14 junctions showing imprecise repair outside coding sequences.
evaluation: Claims C6, C15, C34-C42, C140-C143 provide strong validation evidence through complementary approaches. WGS data (C35-C37, C39) demonstrates genome-wide specificity, though one potential off-target in mNeonGreen-myosinhc could not be confirmed by PCR (C38). Sanger sequencing (C40-C41) confirms precision at junction sites. The combination of methods addresses known limitations of previous validation approaches.

result: Two ubiquitous nuclear marker lines (eGFP-cbx1b and mGL-cbx1b) were generated by targeting the cbx1b locus. These lines express fluorescent reporters in all nuclei of every tissue examined, serving as endogenous ubiquitous nuclear labels in teleosts.
evaluation: Claims C43-C47 describe the generation and characterization of ubiquitous nuclear markers. The choice of cbx1b is justified by prior knowledge (C44, C45). Expression data (C47, n>10 embryos) with imaging evidence demonstrates ubiquitous nuclear labeling across tissues. The result is well-supported by both the experimental approach and characterization data.

result: An mScarlet-pcna fusion protein line was generated with high efficiency (28% F0 mosaic expression, 50% germline transmission). mScarlet-Pcna-positive cells were detected in supra-basal epidermal cells, with a subset showing nuclear speckles characteristic of late S phase.
evaluation: Claims C48-C56 establish the generation and initial characterization of the mScarlet-pcna line. The rationale is supported by extensive prior work on Pcna as a proliferation marker (C49-C53). Experimental data (C54-C56, n=10 embryos) demonstrates expected expression patterns and cell cycle-specific localization (nuclear speckles in late S phase). The characterization is consistent with known Pcna biology.

result: An eGFP-rab11a fusion protein line was generated showing punctate intracellular signal corresponding to trafficking organelles. High expression was detected in spinal cord and neuromasts, with dynamics of intracellular organelle trafficking observed in vivo in epithelial cells and caudal fin.
evaluation: Claims C57-C60 describe generation and characterization of the eGFP-rab11a line. The target choice is justified by prior knowledge of Rab11a function (C57). Imaging data (C58-C60, n=4-6 embryos) demonstrates expected subcellular localization and trafficking dynamics. The characterization provides 'initial evidence' (C60) of utility, appropriately cautious in interpretation.

result: A g3bp1-eGFP KI line was generated that shows cytoplasmic expression under normal conditions but accumulates in cytoplasmic foci (stress granules) upon temperature shock. This behavior is consistent with prior reports in other organisms and demonstrates potential as a real-time in vivo stress granule reporter.
evaluation: Claims C61-C67 establish the g3bp1-eGFP line as a stress granule marker. The rationale is supported by prior knowledge (C62-C63). Experimental data (C64-C65, n=8 embryos) demonstrates expected stress-responsive relocalization, validated by comparison to prior work in other organisms (C66). The conclusion about potential utility (C67) is appropriately stated as inference based on initial characterization.

result: An mNG-myosinhc KI line was generated that exclusively labels muscle cells. The line shows correct incorporation into sarcomeres (A-bands separated by I-bands) and enables in vivo recording of endogenous Myosinhc dynamics during muscle growth for the first time in a vertebrate model.
evaluation: Claims C68-C72 describe the mNG-myosinhc line. The target choice is justified (C69). Imaging data (C70-C71, n>10 embryos) demonstrates muscle-specific expression and correct sarcomere incorporation, validated by comparison to known sarcomere structure. Live imaging (C72, n=9 embryos) demonstrates novel capability. The claim of 'first time' (C72) is appropriately qualified with 'to the best of our knowledge.'

result: A cdh2-eGFP KI line was generated showing cellular membrane expression in neuronal and non-neuronal tissues including spinal cord, eye, notochord, and neuromasts. High expression in notochord cell types, not previously reported in medaka, is consistent with the tissue's mechanical stress requirements.
evaluation: Claims C73-C79 establish the cdh2-eGFP line. The target choice is justified by prior knowledge (C73-C76). Imaging data (C77, n=5 embryos) demonstrates tissue-specific membrane expression. The novel finding of notochord expression (C78) is appropriately contextualized with mechanical stress considerations and supporting citations. Live imaging capability is demonstrated (C79, n=2 embryos).

result: A mapre1b-mScarlet KI line was generated showing wide expression in medaka embryos (epithelial cells, muscle, notochord, neuromasts) with highest expression in spinal cord. Microtubule dynamics in the spinal cord of living embryos were recorded.
evaluation: Claims C80-C83 describe the mapre1b-mScarlet line. The target choice is justified by prior knowledge of microtubule plus-end binding proteins (C80). Imaging data (C82-C83, n=5 embryos) demonstrates expected expression patterns and live recording of microtubule dynamics. The characterization is straightforward and well-supported.

result: The mScarlet-pcna line acts as an organismal-wide marker for proliferative cells. In neuromasts, mScarlet-pcna expression matches the location of proliferative mantle cells (MCs) but not differentiated hair cells or support cells. Neuromast border cells (nBCs) in late S phase (4/42) were observed, providing direct evidence that nBCs retain the ability to divide.
evaluation: Claims C84-C95 validate mScarlet-pcna as a proliferation marker in neuromasts. The experimental approach using double transgenic animals (C85) is appropriate. Expression patterns (C89-C91, n=10 neuromast organs) match prior knowledge of MC proliferation (C88, C90). The novel finding about nBC proliferation (C94-C95) is supported by observation of nuclear speckles indicating late S phase, though the sample size (4/42 cells) is modest.

result: Proliferative cells in the optic tectum are located at the lateral, caudal, and medial edges in a crescent-like topology with graded mScarlet-pcna expression. This pattern is consistent with previous BrdU/IdU staining studies in medaka.
evaluation: Claims C96-C98 describe proliferation patterns in the optic tectum. Imaging data (C96-C97, n=4 embryos) demonstrates spatial organization of proliferative cells. The validation by comparison to prior histological studies (C98) strengthens the result. The characterization is well-supported and appropriately contextualized.

result: In the developing pectoral fin, cells located proximally expressed highest mScarlet-pcna levels with expression decreasing along the proximo-distal axis. This previously unreported pattern provides evidence that the differentiation axis is spatially organized from proximal to distal in medaka.
evaluation: Claims C99-C100 describe a novel proliferation pattern in the pectoral fin. Imaging data (C99, n=4 embryos) demonstrates the proximo-distal gradient. The inference about differentiation axis organization (C100) is reasonable based on the proliferation gradient, though appropriately qualified as not previously reported. The sample size is modest but adequate for initial characterization.

result: Proliferative cells in the spinal cord of stage 40 medaka embryos occur in clusters preferentially located on the dorsal side. The mScarlet-pcna line can be used to uncover proliferation zones in vivo within organs or tissues of interest.
evaluation: Claims C101-C102 describe spinal cord proliferation and summarize the utility of the line. Imaging data (C101, n=4 embryos) demonstrates a previously unreported finding about spinal cord proliferation. The conclusion about utility (C102) is appropriately supported by the multiple tissue characterizations presented. The result is well-supported though sample sizes are modest.

result: The mScarlet-pcna line recapitulates known Pcna dynamics and can be used as an endogenous cell cycle reporter. Tracked epithelial cells showed: decreasing Pcna in G1, increasing Pcna in S phase prior to nuclear speckles (late S phase marker), peak pixel intensity at S/G2 transition, and sharp decrease at M phase onset.
evaluation: Claims C103-C111 validate mScarlet-pcna as a cell cycle reporter. The approach is grounded in extensive prior work (C103-C105, C107-C108, C110). Quantitative tracking data (C106, C109, C110, n=9 epithelial cells) demonstrates all expected cell cycle phase characteristics. The analysis methods (3D surface plots, histograms) are appropriate. The conclusion (C111) is well-supported by the comprehensive characterization matching known Pcna behavior.

result: CRISPR/Cas9 has been used to generate fluorescently labeled fusion proteins by HDR in various species, but HDR-mediated KI efficiencies in vertebrates can be low and the process remains cumbersome. Recent improvements include biotinylated long homology arms, linking donors to Cas9, and shorter homology arms with in vivo plasmid linearization.
evaluation: Claims C1, C8-C13 provide context about prior CRISPR/Cas9 work and its limitations. These are well-supported by extensive citations to prior literature. The assessment of the field (C11) is reasonable given the cited evidence. This background appropriately motivates the current work.

result: Despite CRISPR/Cas9's impact, there is a paucity of validated single-copy fusion protein lines in vertebrates (3 in medaka, handful in zebrafish prior to this work). Previous approaches using plasmid donors with long homology arms face challenges including concatemerization, off-target integration, and require in vivo linearization. PCR-amplified linear donors with short homology arms could be highly effective due to high molar concentration.
evaluation: Claims C112-C120 provide field assessment and rationale for the approach. The paucity of lines (C112-C113) is documented by citations. Problems with previous approaches (C115-C119) are well-supported by extensive citations. The hypothesis about PCR-amplified donors (C120) is reasonable based on molecular considerations, though it remains a hypothesis rather than demonstrated fact.

result: The approach builds on recent improvements (biotinylated primers, synthetic sgRNAs, mSA-tagged Cas9) and is highly efficient, precise, and scalable. PCR amplification eliminates the need for cloning and in vivo linearization, significantly simplifying endogenous protein tagging.
evaluation: Claims C121-C123, C126-C128 describe methodological components and advantages. The use of established improvements (C121-C123) is well-cited. The conclusions about efficiency and simplicity (C126-C128) are supported by the experimental data showing successful generation of 8 lines with high efficiency. The advantages are clearly demonstrated by the methodology and results.

result: Recent work in zebrafish using a similar approach supports that donors with short homology arms are sufficient to drive HDR when in linear dsDNA form. The mechanism may involve synthesis-dependent strand annealing (SDSA), where short homologies (30-40 bp) are sufficient to anneal with chromosomal DNA.
evaluation: Claims C129-C133 provide mechanistic context and comparison to recent work. The zebrafish comparison (C129-C130) is appropriately cited and supports generalizability. The SDSA mechanism (C131-C133) is presented as a hypothesis ('one possible explanation,' C131) and is well-supported by citations to HDR mechanisms. The interpretation is appropriately cautious.

result: Validation of single-copy insertions is complicated with long homology arms due to concatemerization and episome formation. PCR/Sanger sequencing faces technical challenges, junction PCR can produce artifacts, and Southern blotting (the gold standard) has limitations in excluding partial integrations elsewhere. Plasmid donors can lead to unwanted insertions.
evaluation: Claims C134-C139 critique previous validation approaches. The limitations are well-documented by extensive citations to prior work. The assessment is balanced, acknowledging both the gold standard status of Southern blotting (C137) and its limitations (C138). This appropriately motivates the WGS validation approach used in the current work.

result: Eight novel endogenous protein fusion lines significantly expand genetic tools in medaka. Ubiquitous fusion proteins from endogenous loci avoid transgene overexpression and variegation issues. The conserved cbx1b locus could provide an alternative strategy for ubiquitous nuclear markers in other teleosts and serve as a landing site for genetic constructs.
evaluation: Claims C144-C149 summarize the contribution and discuss implications. The generation of 8 lines (C144) is well-documented. The advantages of endogenous expression (C145-C147) are supported by citations about transgene issues. The speculation about applications in other organisms (C148-C149) is appropriately presented as potential future directions with supporting citations.

result: The g3bp1-eGFP line can be used as an in vivo stress marker and to study stress granule formation. High rab11a expression in neuromasts and spinal cord may indicate higher protein turnover. No endogenous myosin KI has been reported in teleosts. The cdh2-eGFP line can be used to study N-cadherin dynamics and EMT processes.
evaluation: Claims C150-C154 discuss applications and context for specific lines. The utility statements (C150, C154) are appropriately supported by the characterization data. The speculation about rab11a expression (C151) is appropriately cautious ('could indicate'). The field assessment about myosin (C152) and N-cadherin's role in EMT (C153) are supported by citations.

result: The mScarlet-pcna line addresses limitations of BrdU/IdU staining (which requires animal sacrifice) and can discover proliferation zones in any tissue. Proof-of-principle evidence shows it acts as a bona fide marker for proliferative zones in various medaka tissues, representing an important tool for stem cell research. A similar strategy could be adopted in other organisms.
evaluation: Claims C155-C162 discuss the significance of the mScarlet-pcna line for stem cell research. The context about stem cell research approaches (C155-C157) is well-supported by citations. The advantages over BrdU/IdU (C157-C158) are clear. The proof-of-principle evidence (C160) is supported by the multiple tissue characterizations. The conclusions about utility (C161) and potential applications (C162) are appropriately supported and qualified.

result: The mScarlet-pcna line can be used as an endogenous cell cycle reporter in medaka, with dynamics correlating to prior work in other vertebrates. This offers advantages over FUCCI systems: no overexpression requirement, avoids variegation/silencing issues, and allows simultaneous use with other fluorescent reporters. Due to Pcna conservation, developing similar reporters in other organisms is attractive.
evaluation: Claims C163-C170 discuss the cell cycle reporter application and advantages. The validation by comparison to prior work (C164) is well-supported by citations. The advantages over FUCCI (C166-C169) are clearly articulated and appropriately supported by citations about transgene issues. The speculation about applications in other organisms (C170) is reasonable given Pcna conservation and is appropriately presented as a possibility.
